cycles.failure: The immutable V2 request reached Google once and returned HTTP 400 with no image.
cycles.root_cause: The V2 serialized image response_format included delivery=inline, while the current official Gemini 3.1 Flash Image Interactions examples omit delivery for inline image bytes.
cycles.repair: Created a fresh V3 approval and authority whose official-SDK serialized response_format contains only type, mime_type, aspect_ratio and image_size; V1 and V2 artifacts remain unchanged.

cycles.failure: The consumed V1 and V2 task authorities cannot authorize another paid request.
cycles.root_cause: Terminal one-shot authorities are intentionally non-reopenable.
cycles.repair: Bound the new operator message digest to a distinct V3 task key, authorization path, run prefix, request hash, prompt hash and serialized body hash with exact-one terminal submit semantics.

cycles.failure: Adding optional V3 preflight fields initially changed how current models reloaded historical V1/V2 hash payloads.
cycles.root_cause: Persisted artifacts and current Pydantic dumps represent later optional null fields differently.
cycles.repair: Selected only the representation-compatible payload variant already committed by each immutable content hash; semantic values remain strict and tampered hashes still fail closed.

cycles.root_cause: Archive roles previously distinguished only V1 and V2.
cycles.repair: Added a distinct 44-role V3 package, preserved frozen V1/V2 role sets, bound V3 authority/serialization/combined immutability/runtime evidence, and created this repair history before any paid submit.

cycles.root_cause: The previous VQC contract assumed every successful provider response supplied an interaction identifier; this successful SDK response supplied hash-bound image bytes and usage but no identifier.
cycles.repair: Kept the paid attempt, authority, budget, provider receipt and image immutable. For V3 success only, derive a truthful evidence URI from the immutable provider-response content hash and use it consistently through materialization, normalization, rights and evaluator checks. V1/V2 still require their explicit IDs.
